title: The Knot and the Dog: Matías Carbone from the ABM Classroom to Avenida Alvear
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Record Begins in the Middle

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the birth no source records
stops.date_confidence: not an event. No birth date, birth year, or birthplace was found in any source reached, and 1999 is used here only because it is the earliest year his record contains. The date is an anchor to the start of the documentation, not to anything that happened.
stops.campa: No document reachable in 2026 gives Matías Carbone a birth date or a birthplace. The brand's own history, the Instagram bio and a LinkedIn snippet all open in 1999 with an enrolment in a fashion school, and none of them says anything about what came before. Apart from two clauses naming France and Japan, Buenos Aires holds every event the record places anywhere: the school, the first atelier, the ten years of menswear, the label, the showroom. The atlas pins him at the city's canonical point. The years before 1999 are entered here as a gap.
suggested_refs: Any Argentine civil register entry or press interview that would date his birth

stops.name: Marcelo T. de Alvear 1155, the fashion school
stops.date_confidence: year attested by two independent sources, the brand's About page and a LinkedIn profile snippet; month and day defaulted to 01. The coordinate is Nominatim's resolution of Marcelo T. de Alvear 1155, correcting an earlier pass that placed the school a kilometre away in Barrio Norte.
stops.campa: He begins fashion studies in 1999. His own page calls the institution Universidad ABM; the school at Marcelo T. de Alvear 1155 is ABM Instituto de Educación Superior en Diseño, which grants a three-year degree in Diseño de Indumentaria and is not a university. A LinkedIn profile repeats the sentence and the year without copying the brand site, which makes 1999 the one date in his biography confirmed twice. The building stands in Retiro, about ten blocks from the showroom he will open twenty-two years later.
stops.quote: Matías Carbone inició sus estudios de moda en 1999 en la Universidad ABM
stops.quote_source: LinkedIn profile snippet, ar.linkedin.com/in/matias-carbone-417a0877, surfaced via html.duckduckgo.com
suggested_refs: ABM Instituto de Educación Superior en Diseño, Marcelo T. de Alvear 1155, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Palermo, the first house of the trade
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The brand page names the post and gives no year and no address; 2000 is placed immediately after the 1999 school start, and the Palermo coordinate is a neighbourhood placement carried over from the label's usual association, not a located studio.
stops.campa: His first work in the trade is at the house of Paula Cahen D'Anvers, an established Buenos Aires designer whose label sells knitwear and womenswear across the country. The brand history gives the post a single line and no dates, and no source places the atelier at a street address; Palermo is a placement rather than a finding. What he learns there is not recorded anywhere. He leaves the workroom for a runway, and the years before Félix are spent being photographed in other people's clothes.
suggested_refs: Paula Cahen D'Anvers company history, which would date and locate the atelier

stops.name: Paris, the modelling years in France
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction on both counts. The source names only the country, France, with no city, agency, client, or year; Paris is the researcher's placeholder for a nation and 2001 is a placement inside the early 2000s. An earlier pass tagged this stop as attested, which overstated a one-clause self-description.
stops.campa: Before he designs professionally he is photographed and walked. The brand history says he modelled in France and Japan and credits those years with teaching him how a garment is built from the inside, which is the only published account of them and was written by him. It names no agency, no city, and no year. Paris stands here for a country. The atlas will bring him back to this same coordinate two decades later as a designer showing menswear, and both visits rest on the same single page.
suggested_refs: Any French agency card or editorial credit from the early 2000s naming Matías Carbone

stops.name: Tokyo, the modelling years in Japan
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The source says only Japon, with no city, agency, or date, and no second document mentions the passage at all; Tokyo is a national placeholder and the year is a placement.
stops.campa: The same modelling years take him to Japan. The source is one clause on his own About page, without a city, an agency, a client, or a date, and nothing else in print mentions it. Tokyo stands in for the nation. Japan returns in the brand's own telling as the first of five export markets, and both statements sit in the same paragraph of the same page, a quarter of a century apart in what they describe. An earlier pass added that Japan shaped his later collections. No source says so, and that sentence is withdrawn here.
suggested_refs: Any Japanese agency record or editorial credit from the early 2000s naming Matías Carbone

stops.name: Buenos Aires, creative director of Félix
stops.date_confidence: the role and the span 2003 to 2013 are stated plainly on the brand's About page; month and day defaulted to 01. The coordinate is the city pin, because no source locates the Félix studio and an earlier pass invented a Palermo coordinate by reasoning from where menswear labels tend to cluster.
stops.campa: He is creative director of the menswear label Félix from 2003 to 2013, the longest post of his working life and the one that makes him a menswear designer rather than a general one. The dates and the role are stated plainly on his own page. Where the studio stood is not. No source locates Félix at any address, and an earlier research pass placed it in Palermo by reasoning from the neighbourhood's concentration of menswear labels, which is not evidence. The pin falls back to the city itself.
suggested_refs: Any trade registry or press notice locating the menswear label Félix in Buenos Aires, 2003-2013

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the consulting years
stops.date_confidence: the span 2013 to 2021 is given by the brand's About page as a single line naming no houses; month and day defaulted to 01. Whether the work was continuous, and whether any of it happened outside Buenos Aires, is not stated by any source.
stops.campa: Between Félix and his own name there are eight years spent consulting for other fashion houses. His About page compresses them into one line and names none of the houses. Nothing else in print mentions the period at all. Which houses, whether the work was continuous, whether it ever took him out of Buenos Aires: none of it is recorded. These eight years are the emptiest stretch in a record thin to begin with, and they end with him founding a label under his own surname.
suggested_refs: Any Argentine fashion-house credit list naming Carbone as consultant between 2013 and 2021

stops.name: Av. Alvear 1807, the label founded
stops.date_confidence: the founding year 2021 is attested by the brand's About page; month and day defaulted to 01. The coordinate is Nominatim's resolution of Avenida Alvear 1807, correcting an earlier estimate that sat about 160 metres off. The page does not say the label was founded at this address, and pinning the founding here is an inference.
stops.campa: In 2021 he founds the label that carries his surname and calls it the most personal project of his career. The About page gives the year; it gives the showroom at Avenida Alvear 1807, Departamento 306, in Recoleta; it does not say the label was founded there, and joining those two facts is an inference and is marked as one. Avenida Alvear runs between the Alvear Palace and the Palacio Duhau, four of the most expensive blocks in the city. He opens on it in the twenty-second year of the working life the record gives him.
sources: ccarbone.com.ar, 'About Carbone' and site-wide address block
suggested_refs: Any Argentine trade registration for the Carbone label, which would date and locate the founding

stops.date_confidence: the season Fall Winter 2021 and the title La Primera are attested by the brand's own season navigation; no presentation date exists in any source, and April is a placement inside the southern autumn rather than a found date.

stops.name: Av. Alvear 1807, the door and its hours
stops.date_confidence: the address and the opening hours are attested twice, on the brand's own About page and in the verified Instagram bio, but neither source dates them; 2021 is carried over from the founding year and the hours are a present-tense fact given a past anchor.

stops.name: Belgrano, the anonymous invitation
stops.date_confidence: the post is dated 31 January and opens with the word ayer, yesterday, which puts the visit on the thirtieth. Two earlier lenses carried the post date as the visit date; the essay's own wording decides it. The coordinate is inherited unchanged from laura_renee_maier.journey.json rather than re-derived.
stops.campa: An anonymous invitation brings the essayist to a studio in Belgrano. The post that records the visit is dated the thirty-first of January and opens with the word ayer, yesterday, which puts the visit on the thirtieth. Carbone works there in knit, crochet, weaving and embroidery, four techniques usually divided among four trades. The atlas already holds this afternoon from the other side: it is a stop in the file of Laura Renée Maier, pinned at this same coordinate, written before Carbone had a file of his own.
stops.quote: Carbone works in knot topology; she works in dog-headed gods.
suggested_refs: Matías Carbone's Belgrano studio, whose street address the essay does not give

stops.name: Belgrano, the collection of the circle and the dog
stops.date_confidence: same visit, dated by the essay's own ayer; the essay describes the collection without naming it or dating its making.
stops.campa: He shows a new collection of clothing, knitted, crocheted, woven and embroidered, and through all of it two figures keep returning: the geometry of the circle and the emblem of the dog. Neither is explained in the essay as a motif chosen for a season. The dog is still there four months later, running through a winter collection, and it is the dog that carries his work into a thread the corpus runs at length: Anubis, the cynocephalus Saint Christopher, a currency named after a Shiba Inu.
suggested_refs: The unnamed knit, crochet, woven and embroidered collection shown in Belgrano, January 2023

stops.name: Belgrano, nodus and the root that binds
stops.date_confidence: same visit. The conversation is attested by the essay; the etymology it relays is checked here against Etymonline and is partly wrong, and the error is flagged rather than corrected, because the corpus is locked and corrections are additions.
stops.campa: The conversation turns to how cloth is made and stays made: knots, nodes, nets, and the word under all of them. Latin nodus descends from the Proto-Indo-European root ned, to bind, and the essay traces nudillo, desnudo, nudo and nodo back to it. Three of the four hold. Desnudo does not: it comes from Latin nudus, which Etymonline assigns to a different root, nogw, naked, the root of Greek gymnos. The false cognate is left standing as the essay wrote it, flagged and uncorrected. Indra's net enters the same conversation as the historical frame for knotted mesh.
suggested_refs: Etymonline on Latin nodus and on Latin nudus, the two roots the essay merges

stops.name: Belgrano, Anubis and the binding of the body
stops.date_confidence: same visit. That Anubis was discussed is attested by the essay; that he was a specialist in knotting the funerary body is not attested by any Egyptological source found, and that half of the claim is reconstruction.
stops.campa: Anubis enters the room. In the essay he is the god who knots the funerary body, binding the dead in linen so that they keep their shape; Egyptology attests him as the god of embalming and mummification and gives no source making him a specialist in knots. The knot is the essayist's own addition, and it is what puts a dog-headed god in a room with a knitwear designer. The atlas keeps that dog head in three other files: San Cristóbal the cynocephalus, Gustave Flaubert's procession of gods, and Laura Renée Maier's black-thread diptych.
suggested_refs: Egyptological treatments of Anubis as god of embalming, which do not mention knotting

stops.name: Belgrano, the embroidered Anubis called Christophia
stops.date_confidence: same visit; the closing scene of the post, dated by the same ayer.
stops.campa: The visit ends in front of an embroidered Anubis in a work called Christophia. The essay says the piece was presentada por Laura Renée Maier, presented by her, which is not the same as made by her, and an earlier pass turned the one into the other. The essayist writes that he cannot untangle the threads of this Gordian knot, and that the work rhymes with his own skyrmion cloths. One man works in knot topology and the other in dog-headed gods, and her canvas is hanging in his room, in a city the corpus never says she is in.
stops.quote: Terminamos nuestra conversación mirando la representación bordada de Anubis en la obra titulada Christophia presentada por Laura Renée Maier.
suggested_refs: The work Christophia, whose maker the essay does not name

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the winter collection of the Shiba Inu
stops.date_confidence: the post is dated; the collection it describes is not, and no source says where or whether the garments were shown or sold. The city pin is used because the post describes no visit and no venue.
stops.campa: By May a winter collection is finished and its signature material is a dog. A Shiba Inu runs, chases birds, watches the sky, and guards a secret; the essayist calls it a sun dog. Nothing in the record says where the collection was shown or whether it was sold, only that it existed and that its imagery was read this way in public four months after the studio visit. The circle and the dog he laid out in Belgrano in January have become one animal by the end of autumn.
suggested_refs: The winter 2023 Shiba Inu collection, undocumented outside the corpus

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the face of the generation
stops.date_confidence: the post is dated. The Talmudic passage is verified verbatim on Sefaria; the essay's dating of it to the fifth century is the essayist's own and is not the scholarly dating, and the discrepancy is carried rather than resolved.
stops.campa: The same post sets the collection beside a line from tractate Sotah: in the footsteps of the Messiah, the face of the generation will be like the face of a dog. Sefaria returns the passage verbatim. The essayist dates it to the fifth century; the dictum is mishnaic, tannaitic material of roughly the second or third century, quoted inside a Babylonian Talmud redacted around five hundred to six hundred. Between the prophecy and the Shiba Inu he sets the Dogecoin symbol. The reading is his own and is marked as his own.
stops.quote: The face of the generation will be like the face of a dog.
stops.quote_source: Babylonian Talmud, Sotah 49b, Sefaria translation of פְּנֵי הַדּוֹר כִּפְנֵי הַכֶּלֶב
suggested_refs: Mishnah Sotah 9:15, the tannaitic source of the dictum quoted at Sotah 49b

stops.name: La Verna, the mountain in the embroidery
stops.date_confidence: the post is dated; the mountain is a place the post reaches through an image, not a place anyone travels to in 2023. Nothing suggests Carbone was ever there, and the stop is the essay's geography rather than his.
stops.campa: The post travels to a mountain in Tuscany. Ekaterina Sinchinova's embroidery reveals La Verna, the refuge of Francis of Assisi, stitched over an image of the Dogecoin blockchain that carries the sun dog's face. The essayist reaches Francis through his mother, called in late tradition Pica di Bourlemont, a noblewoman said to come from Provence; the attribution is poorly attested, and her Bourlemont is not the Lorraine family that anchors the corpus's Joan of Arc thread. The English version of the same post calls the artist Ekaterina Vates.
suggested_refs: The sanctuary of La Verna, Chiusi della Verna, Tuscany

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the post the nodus essays do not use
stops.date_confidence: not an event in his life. This is a structural fact about the corpus, anchored to the later of the two posts that name him; the concordance file itself is undated in its listing.
stops.campa: A fact about the corpus rather than about the man. The studio-visit post is not among the hundred and forty-two Instagram posts that the fifty-two numbered nodus essays draw on; the concordance file lists it under the posts not used. The essay sequence that takes its name from the word nodus, knot, does not use the one post in which the author sits in a studio and traces that word to its root with a designer who ties knots for a living. An earlier pass got this right and counted it wrong, saying fifty-two posts where fifty-two counts essays.
suggested_refs: The concordance _nodus_match.md, section 'Instagram essays NOT in the nodus corpus'

stops.name: Av. Alvear 1807, Fall Winter 2024 called Los Pompones
stops.date_confidence: the season and the title are attested by a page that loads, unlike most of the season pages; no presentation date appears anywhere, and April is a placement inside the southern autumn.
stops.campa: The Fall Winter 2024 collection is called Los Pompones. Its page is reachable, unlike most of the season pages, and gives the season, the title, and the Alvear address; it gives no presentation date, so the year is all the date there is. A pompom is a knot of cut yarn with nothing inside it, the simplest object in the whole vocabulary of the trade, and he names a winter after it. The pattern set by La Primera holds: an article, a plain noun, and nothing else.

stops.name: Av. Alvear 1807, Fall Winter 2026 called El Circo
stops.date_confidence: the collection page loads in full and gives the title, the count of designs, the garment types, and the campaign photographer; it gives no presentation date, and April is a placement inside the southern autumn.
stops.campa: Fall Winter 2026 is El Circo, and this page is whole. Ninety designs stage the circus: audacious colour against classical tailoring, high-waisted trousers, silk shirts, the campaign photographed by Cecilia Glik O'Higgins. The brand's own line for it is theatricality as language and contrast as identity. It is the fullest description of any Carbone collection in any source reached, and it comes from the seller rather than from a critic, which is true of nearly everything that is known about his clothes.

segments.name: The Threads Already in the Atlas

stops.name: 8 Red Lion Square, embroidery enters the trade list
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Firm's own founding date, and inherited unchanged from elizabeth_bessie_burden.journey.json rather than re-derived.
stops.campa: Morris, Marshall, Faulkner and Company opens at 8 Red Lion Square with embroidery among its founding trades, and the embroidery is worked by women whose names the firm does not sell: Jane Morris, Elizabeth Burden, later May Morris. It is the oldest node of the thread the atlas files Carbone inside, the one in which cloth worked by hand is treated as art rather than as trade. A hundred and sixty years later a Buenos Aires designer knits, crochets, weaves and embroiders under his own surname, and signs the surname to all four.
sources: J. W. Mackail, The Life of William Morris (1899)
suggested_refs: The trade list of Morris, Marshall, Faulkner and Company, 1861

stops.name: Paris, Flaubert's procession of gods
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day defaulted to 01, and the coordinate is inherited unchanged from gustave_flaubert.journey.json.
stops.campa: Flaubert publishes the third Tentation de saint Antoine, and the hermit's night brings him heresiarchs, the Queen of Sheba, Nebuchadnezzar on all fours eating grass, Vishnu, and the dog-headed Anubis, the whole catalogue of gods walking past one sleepless man. The atlas keeps the stop at the Paris pin. It is the same god the essayist and Carbone stand in front of in Belgrano a hundred and forty-nine years later, embroidered in black thread on a canvas neither of them can account for.
sources: Gustave Flaubert, La Tentation de saint Antoine (1874)
suggested_refs: La Tentation de saint Antoine, third version, 1874

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the blue thread
stops.date_confidence: undated in every source: biographers place the onset of the practice anywhere across the 1940s to the 1960s, and the year is a placeholder inside that range, inherited unchanged from arthur_bispo_do_rosario.journey.json.
stops.campa: In the Colônia Juliano Moreira outside Rio de Janeiro, Arthur Bispo do Rosário unpicks discarded Navy uniforms thread by thread and embroiders with what he pulls out: words, maps, saints, the names of cities, columns of counted things. No document says when the practice begins. It is the atlas's plainest case for embroidery used as a record and not as decoration, and it sits behind the later stitchers in this file, among them a designer who works four textile trades at once and reads his own knots as etymology.
suggested_refs: The embroidered mantle and banners of Arthur Bispo do Rosário, Museu Bispo do Rosário

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the friend's house
stops.date_confidence: the year of the meeting is attested by both artists' accounts; month and day defaulted to 01, and the coordinate is the atlas's canonical Buenos Aires pin, shared with Victoria Ocampo, Borges and Mario Palanti.
stops.campa: Leo Chiachio and Daniel Giannone meet at a friend's house in Buenos Aires and begin, from that year, to embroider a single household: the two of them, their dogs, an invented family, stitched at enormous scale onto cloth over months of hand labour. It is the same year Carbone takes over the menswear house Félix, in the same city. The two practices run for two decades a few kilometres apart, both of them stitching dogs, and no document connects them. The atlas pins both at this coordinate.
stops.quote: the two of them, their dogs, an invented family, stitched at enormous scale onto cloth
suggested_refs: Chiachio and Giannone's early household embroideries, from 2003

stops.name: Aubusson, second place in the oldest tradition
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the prize record; month and day defaulted to 01, and the coordinate is inherited unchanged from daniel_giannone.journey.json.
stops.campa: Chiachio and Giannone take second prize at the Cité Internationale de la Tapisserie in Aubusson, inside the oldest weaving tradition in France. The atlas notes that the crossing echoes the Buenos Aires to Le Havre route in the file of Louis Vuitton. It is the direction a Buenos Aires textile practice travels when it is recognised abroad, and it is the same direction Carbone's brand claims to travel twice a year, out of a Recoleta apartment toward a Paris showing that no French record confirms.
stops.quote: the Buenos Aires to Le Havre crossing in the file of Louis Vuitton
suggested_refs: Cité Internationale de la Tapisserie, Aubusson, 2013 prize record

stops.name: Bogotá, the dog-headed panel
stops.date_confidence: the corpus dates the diptych to 2022 without month or day and names no city for its making; the Bogotá residence pin is inherited unchanged from laura_renee_maier.journey.json, where the same placement is already flagged as reused.
stops.campa: Laura Renée Maier embroiders a diptych in black thread: a nude figure with the head of a dog, gesturing toward its counterpart, Anubis and the cynocephalus Saint Christopher at once, its nimbus carrying the last sixteen bytes of a hash. The corpus dates it 2022 and names no city for its making. A year later one of its panels is on a wall in Belgrano, and Carbone and the essayist are standing in front of it while the essayist writes that he cannot untangle the threads of this Gordian knot.
stops.quote: No puedo entender desenredar los hilos de este nudo Gordiano.
suggested_refs: The Christophia diptych, Anubis and the cynocephalus in black thread

stops.name: San Telmo, the museum takes the embroidery in
stops.date_confidence: the holding is attested by encyclopaedia entries; no acquisition year is given in any source reached, so the date anchors the record's present rather than an event. The coordinate is inherited unchanged from daniel_giannone.journey.json, which reconciled two earlier disagreeing entries.
stops.campa: The Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires, on Avenida San Juan in San Telmo, holds Chiachio and Giannone in its permanent collection, and no acquisition year is given in any source reached. It is where the city's institutions keep embroidery once they have decided embroidery is art. Carbone's cloth is not there and is not meant to be: it is sold from an apartment on Avenida Alvear by appointment, in hours printed on a website. The two buildings stand four kilometres and one category apart.
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires'
suggested_refs: MAMBA accession records, which would date the acquisition

segments.name: What the Record Does Not Hold

stops.name: Belgrano, two addresses for one designer
stops.date_confidence: not an event. The contradiction is stated at the record's present. Belgrano is attested for January 2023 by the essay; Avenida Alvear 1807 is attested as the standing address by the brand's page and Instagram bio; nothing dates a move between them.
stops.campa: Two addresses stand in his file and neither cancels the other. The essay of January 2023 puts his studio in Belgrano; the brand's page and Instagram bio give Avenida Alvear 1807 in Recoleta, eight kilometres southeast, as the standing address of the label. Nothing dates a move, and a working studio and a showroom need not be the same room. A neighbouring file in the atlas already records one bad Belgrano gloss laid on a Recoleta address, so both pins are kept here and the contradiction is left open.
suggested_refs: Any source dating a move between the Belgrano studio and the Alvear showroom

stops.name: Av. Alvear 1807, the account and its drifting count
stops.date_confidence: the verified account, the Threads link, and the bio are attested on the fetch date given; the follower count moved between two consecutive daily fetches and is deliberately not stated as a figure.
stops.campa: The account is verified and carries a link to Threads under the same handle. An earlier pass wrote down 34.8K followers as a fact; a re-fetch a day later returned 34.9K, which is what a follower count is worth in a record meant to last. The number is dropped and the account is kept. What the account holds is the only continuous public run of his work, seasonal collections presented as posts, and it matters because the site keeps the names of the seasons and returns 404 for nearly everything else.
suggested_refs: The @matiascarbone Instagram archive, the only continuous record of the collections

stops.name: Buenos Aires, press claimed and press unread
stops.date_confidence: not an event. This is the state of the search at the close of research: the coverage is claimed by highlight titles on his own account, no article was read, and the session's web-search quota was exhausted before a proper press search could run.
stops.campa: His Instagram highlight titles claim coverage by Ángeles y Demonios, Telenotas, and La Nación. No article was read. A guessed La Nación address returned a 404, and the session's search budget was spent before a proper press search could run, so what is recorded is the brand's claim of having been covered and not the coverage itself. One search route did work: a DuckDuckGo HTML query returned a LinkedIn profile and a Facebook page, both repeating the 1999 ABM line, which corroborates his training and nothing else.
suggested_refs: Any La Nación, Telenotas, or Ángeles y Demonios item on Carbone, none of which was located

stops.name: Belgrano, the queue entry and the reason for it
stops.date_confidence: the census file is dated 2026-08-02 in its filename; the queue entry it accompanies is undated, and both are records about the atlas rather than about him.
stops.campa: The atlas's own census of real persons lists him with three documents and calls him an artist collaborator with studio in Belgrano, Buenos Aires. The queue entry names the reason he was approved for research: a direct interlock with the corpus's own embroidery-art thread and its nodus knot material. He is a living designer in the middle of his seasons: no tomb, no editions, no posthumous legend, no rediscovery. The frame the atlas usually reserves for an afterlife does not apply to him and is left empty.
stops.quote: artist collaborator with studio in Belgrano, Buenos Aires
suggested_refs: QUEUE.md line 305, the brief that commissioned this file
